title: Bounded ordered monomials span cyclotomic type-A Hecke algebras
statement: Over any commutative base ring $A$ with invertible nondegenerate parameter, use the defining relations of [[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]], writing $q_H$ for the nondegenerate Hecke parameter. For a monic degree-$\ell>0$ cyclotomic polynomial $f$, with unit constant term in the nondegenerate branch, the quotient by $f(X_1)=0$ is spanned by $X_1^{a_1}\cdots X_d^{a_d}T_w$, and the degenerate quotient by $f(x_1)=0$ is spanned by $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_d^{a_d}w$, where $0\le a_r<\ell$ and $w\in S_d$. In particular, over a field F each quotient has dimension at most $\ell^d d!$. This applies to $f(t)=\prod_{i\in I}(t-q_H^i)^{\lambda_i}$ and $f(t)=\prod_{i\in I}(t-i)^{\lambda_i}$ in the two finite-quantum-characteristic branches, with $\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i$. No independence or separate relation $f(X_r)=0$ or $f(x_r)=0$ for $r>1$ is asserted. If $\ell=0,d>0$, the relation $1=0$ gives the zero algebra with empty spanning family; for $d=0$ the algebra is $A$ with singleton empty monomial.
strategy:
## Elementary straightening input

Only spanning by affine ordered monomials is needed. Move a polynomial past a simple generator using

- NG: T_r p=(s_r p)T_r−(q_H−1)X_{r+1}(p−s_r p)/(X_r−X_{r+1});
- DG: s_r p=(s_r p)s_r−(p−s_r p)/(x_r−x_{r+1}).

Here the first s_r on each right side permutes variables. Both divided differences are polynomials; the NG identity preserves total polynomial degree and the DG correction lowers it by one. The identities follow for a generator variable directly from the mixed relations, and the product case follows by the divided-difference product rule; induction gives every polynomial. Commute distant generators, braid adjacent generators, and reduce quadratic squares to obtain a linear combination of the finite standard words T_w (respectively w). The needed finite Coxeter reduced-word/Hecke straightening supplier is independent of cyclotomic basis or BK. Independence of the affine words is not used.

In NG inverse variables do not present a problem: f(X_1)=0 has nonzero constant term, so X_1^{-1} is a polynomial in X_1. Also X_r=q_H^{1−r}T_{r−1}⋯T_1 X_1 T_1⋯T_{r−1}; inversion expresses X_r^{-1} using X_1^{-1} and T_i^{-1}=q_H^{-1}(T_i−q_H+1). Thus the quotient is generated by positive X's and T's. The positive-polynomial straightening just proved applies.

## NG transported relations and terminating reduction

Put R_1=f(X_1) and R_{r+1}=T_r R_r T_r. Every R_r is zero in the quotient. Ordered straightening gives

R_r=q_H^{r−1}X_r^ℓ+Σ_{a,w} c_{a,w}X_1^{a_1}⋯X_r^{a_r}T_w,

where w∈S_r, Σ_j a_j≤ℓ, and a_r<ℓ. No variable with index above r occurs. Prove this by induction. For a positive integer m, direct summation of the mixed relation gives

T_r X_r^m T_r=q_H X_{r+1}^m−(q_H−1)Σ_{k=1}^{m−1}X_r^k X_{r+1}^{m−k}T_r.

For m=0, T_r²=(q_H−1)T_r+q_H. Hence transporting the displayed leading term produces exactly q_H^r X_{r+1}^ℓ and terms of X_{r+1}-degree below ℓ. For an old remainder monomial, its coefficient has X_r-degree a_r<ℓ. All variables below r commute with T_r, while its T_w lies in the finite H_r and commutes with X_{r+1}. The formula for T_r X_r^{a_r}, followed by finite Hecke straightening of the words T_r T_w T_r and T_w T_r, yields X_{r+1}-degree at most a_r<ℓ. Total degree stays at most ℓ. This proves the induction without assigning f to every X_r.

Order exponent vectors lexicographically as (a_d,a_{d−1},…,a_1), with larger first differing coordinate larger. This is a well-order on N^d and is preserved by addition. If a_r≥ℓ, multiply the zero relation R_r on the left by X^{a−ℓ e_r} and on the right by T_w. Its leading term is q_H^{r−1}X^a T_w. All other terms have the same coordinates above r and a strictly smaller r coordinate, regardless of increases below r. Finite Hecke straightening changes no dot exponents. Since q_H^{r−1} is invertible, solve for X^a T_w in terms of smaller exponent vectors. Well-founded induction terminates and expresses it using only vectors with every coordinate below ℓ. This proves actual bounded ordered spanning.

## DG transported relations and terminating reduction

Put R_1=f(x_1), R_{r+1}=s_r R_r s_r. Straightening and induction show

R_r=x_r^ℓ+Σ_{a,w}c_{a,w}x^a w,

where w∈S_r, all occurring variables have index at most r, and Σ_j a_j<ℓ. Indeed conjugation transports the leading x_r^ℓ to x_{r+1}^ℓ plus correction terms of degree ℓ−1, because

s_r x_r^m s_r=x_{r+1}^m−Σ_{k=0}^{m−1}x_r^k x_{r+1}^{m−1−k}s_r.

Every old remainder remains of degree below ℓ under straightening. If a_r≥ℓ, multiply R_r by x^{a−ℓ e_r} and w; solve for x^a w. Each remainder has total degree strictly below Σ a_j. Induction on total degree proves bounded ordered spanning. In particular this does not falsely claim f(x_r)=0: for level one f(t)=t, x_1=0 implies x_2=s_1, consistently with the formula.

references.title: Brundan and Kleshchev, Blocks of cyclotomic Hecke algebras and Khovanov-Lauda algebras, arXiv:0808.2032v4
references.locator: Sections 3 and 4: presentations and stated basis contracts; the full local argument here is the explicit construction, not a cited basis-proof replacement.

axiom_use: None: polynomial straightening, finite word reductions and well-founded induction are choice-free.

title: The regular Hom norm gives the total cyclotomic KLR dimension in cyclic type A
statement: Let $F$ be any field, $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ with finite $e\ge2$, and use the standard homogeneous cyclotomic KLR quotient at $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i\Lambda_i$ for the cyclic affine type-A Cartan datum and admissible graded parameters. Put $\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i$ and $B_d=\bigoplus_{\operatorname{ht}\beta=d}R^\Lambda(\beta)$. Then $\dim_F B_d=\ell^d d!$ for $d>0$, and $B_0=F$ has dimension one. The proof uses the basic first induction-restriction adjunction and mixed relations on projective $K_0$ modulo $v-1$, where $v$ is the formal grading variable, independent of any Hecke parameter $q_H$. No Frobenius theorem, tensor-form perfectness, highest-weight/global-basis isometry or Hecke basis is required. If $\ell=0,d>0$, then $B_d=0$.
strategy:
Proof. Work in projective K0 modulo v−1, so shifts are identified. Write P_d=[B_d], P_0=[F], D=Σ_i F_i^basic, E=Σ_i E_i^basic. All sums are finite. For A=R^Λ(β), B=R^Λ(β+i), and the right-append corner e=e(β,i), multiplication gives Be⊗_A A≅Be with inverse b↦b⊗1_A. This uses only the unital corner homomorphism A→eBe, not its injectivity. For fixed rank d, the e(β,i) over all β,i are orthogonal and sum to 1_{B_d}; each word has exactly one last color and prefix root. Thus ⊕_{β,i}B_de(β,i)=B_d and P_d=DP_{d−1}=D^dP_0. The zero-corner case gives Be=0 and is included.

The actual same-color categorical decomposition, forgetting its grading shifts, gives [E_i,F_i]=h_i(Λ−β)·Id on root component β for either sign of h_i. Its positive identity summands contribute h_i copies, its negative identity summands contribute the signed counterpart. The unequal-color mixed relation gives [E_i,F_j]=0 for i≠j after its shift is forgotten. Equivalently these are the integral v=1 mixed relations: [h_i]_v specializes to the integer h_i; there is no division by v−v^{-1}. For affine type A every Cartan column sums to zero, also for the double-edge e=2 matrix. Hence Σ_i h_i(Λ−β)=Σ_i λ_i−Σ_j β_jΣ_i a_{ij}=ℓ at every root component. Therefore [E,D]=ℓ·Id. Since rank-zero restriction is zero, EP_0=0. Expanding [E,D^d] gives EP_d=dℓ P_{d−1}.

For finite graded projectives define h(P,Q)=dim_F Hom(P,Q) with grading forgotten, equivalently evaluate the total graded Hom Hilbert series at v=1. Every ungraded map between these finite graded modules is the finite sum of its homogeneous parts. This integer-valued pairing is additive in both variables and unchanged by shifts, so descends to the stated K0 quotient. Pair distinct root blocks by zero and sum over each fixed rank. Ordinary tensor-Hom adjunction F_i^basic⊣E_i^basic gives h(F_iP,Q)=h(P,E_iQ), hence h(DP,Q)=h(P,EQ). All restricted modules remain finite projectives by the actual projectivity clauses, so the recurrence is inside the declared group. Now

h(P_d,P_d)=h(DP_{d−1},P_d)=h(P_{d−1},EP_d)=dℓ·h(P_{d−1},P_{d−1}).

The initial value is h(P_0,P_0)=dim_F End_F(F)=1. Finally End_{B_d}(B_d)≅B_d^op by right multiplication, so h(P_d,P_d)=dim_F B_d. Induction gives dim_F B_d=ℓ^d d! as an ordinary integer. Nothing reduces the integer dimension or dℓ inside F, so the argument includes every field characteristic. For ℓ=0,d>0 the recurrence gives B_d=0. For d=0, independently of ℓ, B_0=F and its basis is the singleton empty monomial; no 0^0 convention is required.

references.title: Kang and Kashiwara, Categorification of Highest Weight Modules via Khovanov-Lauda-Rouquier Algebras, arXiv:1102.4677v4
references.locator: Sections 4–6: projectivity, first adjunction and signed categorical mixed relations; the local dimension recurrence below is supplied explicitly.

axiom_use: None: ordinary first adjunction, finite projective decompositions and integer-valued Hom recurrence introduce no choice.

title: Ordered monomials form a basis of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra
statement: Let $F$ be any field and let $H_d^{\rm deg}$ be the algebra generated by commuting $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ and symmetric-group generators $s_1,\ldots,s_{d-1}$ with $s_rx_r=x_{r+1}s_r-1$, $s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1$, and $s_rx_j=x_js_r$ for $j\notin\{r,r+1\}$, together with the symmetric-group quadratic, braid and distant commutation relations. Then $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_d^{a_d}w:a_j\ge0,\ w\in S_d\}$ is an $F$-basis. This uses only the degenerate presentation clause of [[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]]; no cyclotomic basis or BK isomorphism is assumed. For $d=0$ the basis is the singleton empty monomial.
